--- **📖 Ecosystem knowledge base** — measured data, not marketing: [plugin development guide · plugin-selection data · maintenance criteria](https://perrylink.github.io/dsh-plugin-guide/). ## ⭐ 如果它帮到了你 这个插件是 [DSH 插件家族](https://github.com/PerryLink)的一员（40+ 个，全部 Apache-2.0）。如果你在用，**给个 star** —— 它不会解锁任何功能，但会让下一个人在搜索里更容易找到它。 *English:* part of a 40+ plugin family for DeepSeek Harness. If it is useful, **a star helps the next person find it** — nothing is gated behind it. ## What is dsh-permission-rules? Claude Code-style declarative permission rules for DeepSeek Harness. Rules decide what is known. A reviewer model decides what is not. ![Terminal demo of dsh-permission-rules: dsh-permission-rules — deny/ask rules in one YAML file](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PerryLink/dsh-permission-rules/main/docs/assets/dsh-permission-rules-demo.png) ![Animated terminal demo of dsh-permission-rules](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PerryLink/dsh-permission-rules/main/docs/assets/dsh-permission-rules-demo.gif) *The same run, animated.* ## Compatibility | Surface | Status | |---|---| | Harness | DeepSeek Harness `dsh-v0.2.1-alpha.1` (adapted 2026-09-22, full gate chain): its plugin config is the live settings contract — every field is declared `.volatile()`, the Loader hands `apply` a live reference per field, and a saved edit is committed into the running references WITHOUT remounting the plugin, with out-of-range values refused by the schema before anything is written. A host whose Schemastery predates `volatile()` (before 3.18.3) still mounts and runs this plugin — the fields simply stay ordinary values and the live config form is unavailable — because the marker is applied through a capability probe rather than assumed. `Session.append` on this line still cannot stamp the `ignorable` marker (its third argument is the surface-intent bag, and the envelope field survives for stored-log reads only), so the whole `0.2-alpha` line is pre-checked as unmarked and session-log audit stays disabled by default — `append` reads only `sourceEventSeqs`/`surfaceOp` and freezes the envelope, so it has no code path that could stamp the marker; the earlier `0.1.7-alpha` (adapted 2026-09-22), `0.1.5-rc.2` (adapted 2026-09-09) and `0.1.3-alpha` lines keep the same surface-only append signature, and every `0.2` prerelease is classified with them (a STABLE `0.2.x` release is left to the append probe, so a restored marker surface is adopted without a new plugin release). Those lines' log migrations refuse unclassified plugin events even when marked, so `strip` v1 audit rows before a `0.1.3-alpha` host opens the log and v2 audit rows before a `0.1.5-alpha` host migrates it (native v3 logs only need `repair`). | | Node | `^22.19.0 || >=24.0.0` | | Platforms | All (host + web settings client) | | Model | Any (deny/ask reasons surface through tool results) | ## What you get `dsh-permission-rules` puts an ordered **`allow` / `deny` / `ask`** rule list in front of every tool call on the `tools/pre-execute` waterfall — deterministic, instant, auditable, and written by you in plain YAML: - **`deny`** blocks the call; the rule's `reason` becomes the model-visible error. - **`ask`** rides the official approval seam (mount `dsh-auto-review` for a second-model answerer, or a human answers; with neither, the harness fails closed). - **`allow`** (and no-match) strictly delegates via `next()` — downstream listeners are never short-circuited. Every hit **and** every passthrough is audit-logged as a `permissionRules/decision` session event (log-only — nothing extra is injected into the model context). - **Rich matching** — tool-name globs (including `mcp__*`), agent-identity selectors (`main` / `subagent` / `preset:*`), argument key/value globs **or** regexes (with `!pattern` negation and an `absent` key dimension), workspace-relative path globs at **any nesting depth**, `when` host conditions (env vars, platform), and **shell command decomposition** (`argv`: command word, argument tokens, pipeline signature) for token-precise command matching. - **Built-in high-risk baseline** — a shipped deny/ask ruleset (destructive commands, privilege escalation, download-and-execute, sensitive paths) enabled by default and appended after user rules so a nearer user rule can override it; toggle with `builtin.enabled`. - **Hierarchical rule files** — optional `searchUp` merges every `.dsh/rules.yaml` from the session cwd to the filesystem root, nearest first. - **Dry-run rollout** — `enforce: false` audits what the policy *would* do while passing every call through. - **Hot reload** — Chokidar watch with debounce; a broken edit keeps the previous rules, never crashes. On a WSL host, or for a rule file under `/mnt/`, the watch switches to polling because native change events are unreliable there. - **Fail loud** — invalid YAML, unknown actions/fields, bad globs/regexes, backtracking-prone patterns, or more than `maxRules` rules fail the load. ## Rule syntax ```yaml # /.dsh/rules.yaml rules: - match: { tools: [bash, pwsh], params: { command: "git push*" }, paths: ["**/secrets/**"] } action: deny reason: "No pushes from protected paths" - match: { tools: [edit, write] } action: ask reason: "File writes need confirmation" ``` - **Match dimensions** — `tools` (globs, incl. `mcp__*`), `agents` (`main` / `subagent` / `preset:`; unknown identity never matches — fail closed), `params` (key/value globs or regexes, `!pattern` negation, `absent` key dimension), `paths` (workspace-relative globs extracted at any nesting depth), `when` (`env` var globs/regexes + a closed `platform` list), and `network` (`domains` / `ips` / `ports` / `schemes` — globs, wildcards, CIDRs, port ranges). - **Actions** — `allow` / `deny` / `ask`, evaluated in file order, first match wins. - **Rule metadata** — `enabled: false` (visible but inert), `description`, `tags`; unknown fields fail the load. - **Schema**

plugins.description: Semantic session search backend for DSH, backed by Ollama or any OpenAI-compatible embedding endpoint.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-session-query-vector

A semantic session-search backend for DSH, backed by Ollama or any OpenAI-compatible `/v1/embeddings` endpoint.

DSH ships a SQLite full-text backend (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-session-query-sqlite`) that answers "which session contained this word". This package replaces it with a vector backend that answers "which session was about this" — you ask in your own words, the query is embedded, and the closest chunks come back with their session and snippet.

It is a drop-in replacement for the official backend: both extend the same `sessionQuery` service, so exactly one of them may be mounted at a time.

## Requirements

| | |
|---|---|
| DSH | `0.2.1-rc.2` (developed and tested against it) |
| `@deepseek-ai/cordis` | `~4.0.5` |
| `@deepseek-ai/schemastery` | `3.18.5` (ships with DSH) |
| Node.js | 22+ — the indexer uses the built-in `node:sqlite` (`DatabaseSync`) |
| An embedding endpoint | Ollama locally, or any OpenAI-compatible API |

Earlier DSH releases are untested.

## Two pieces

| Piece | What it is |
|---|---|
| `lib/index.js` | The **query** side — a `SessionQueryEngine` subclass mounted as a plugin. Answers searches by reading the index. Never embeds. |
| `indexer.mjs` | The **index** side — a standalone script. Walks `~/.dsh/sessions`, embeds the message text, writes the vectors. |

They are deliberately separate: search must stay fast, and embedding is slow. The query side never triggers an embedding on the search path; if the index is empty it returns nothing.

**The two sides must use the same embedding model.** Otherwise the stored vectors and the query vector live in different spaces and every score is noise. Configure `embedModel` identically in both.

## Install

```bash
dsh plugin --profile <your-profile> add github:minhaoli/dsh-session-query-vector
```

The package declares `dsh.bundle.patch`, so `dsh plugin add` appends it to `dsh.profile.bundles` and the loader mounts it on the next start.

**The bundle patch also disables the official backend**, because both register `sessionQuery`:

```yaml
# cordis.patch.yml shipped with this package
- id: session-query-sqlite
  disabled: true

- insert:
    - id: session-query-vector
      name: 'dsh-session-query-vector'
      config:
        provider: ollama
        baseUrl: 'http://127.0.0.1:11434'
        embedModel: bge-m3
        openAt: first-search
```

If you would rather keep the official backend, remove that first row and do not mount this package — they cannot coexist.

## Configuration

Set these in your profile's `cordis.patch.yml`. A patch replaces the targeted row's whole `config` rather than merging into it, so restate every key you want to keep.

```yaml
# ~/.dsh/profiles/<profile>/cordis.patch.yml
- insert:
    - id: session-query-vector
      name: 'dsh-session-query-vector'
      config:
        path: 'C:/Users/<you>/.dsh/storages/session-query-vector.sqlite'
        provider: openai
        baseUrl: 'https://api.siliconflow.cn/v1'
        apiKey: 'sk-...'
        embedModel: 'BAAI/bge-m3'
        openAt: first-search
        topK: 20
        minScore: 0.45
```

| Key | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `path` | `~/.dsh/storages/session-query-vector.sqlite` | Index database. Created on first use. |
| `openAt` | `first-search` | `startup` opens the DB at mount; `first-search` on the first query; `never` disables search entirely. |
| `provider` | `ollama` | `ollama` or `openai`. `openai` means any OpenAI-compatible `/v1/embeddings`. |
| `baseUrl` | `http://127.0.0.1:11434` | Embedding endpoint. A trailing `/v1` is stripped and re-added, so `https://host/v1` and `https://host` both work. |
| `apiKey` | `""` | Sent as `Authorization: Bearer` when non-empty. Not needed for Ollama. |
| `embedModel` | `bge-m3` | Must match the indexer. |
| `embedTimeoutMs` | `120000` | Per-request timeout. |
| `topK` | `20` | Candidates pulled from the index before ranking. |
| `minScore` | `0.45` | Cosine floor. |
| `relMargin` | `0.10` | Relative cutoff: a hit is kept only if its score is within `relMargin` of the best hit. |
| `snippetChars` | `240` | Snippet length in the result. |
| `readWindowMax` | `50` | Read window for the engine's live-preferred reads. |

## Endpoint contracts

### Ollama (`provider: ollama`)

```http
POST {baseUrl}/api/embeddings
content-type: application/json

{ "model": "bge-m3", "prompt": "the text to embed" }
```

Response: `{ "embedding": [0.013, -0.021, ...] }`.

Pull the model first:

```bash
ollama pull bge-m3
```

### OpenAI-compatible (`provider: openai`)

```http
POST {baseUrl}/v1/embeddings
authorization: Bearer <apiKey>
content-type: application/json

{ "model": "BAAI/bge-m3", "input": ["chunk one", "chunk two"] }
```

Response: `{ "data": [{ "index": 0, "embedding": [...] }, ...] }`. Results are sorted by `data[].index` before use — some providers return them out of order.

A trailing `/v1` on `baseUrl` is stripped before `/v1/embeddings` is appended, so `https://api.siliconflow.cn/v1` does not become `/v1/v1/embeddings`.

Any endpoint that satisfies this contract works: SiliconFlow, OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, Together, a local vLLM or LM Studio server, and so on. Set `baseUrl`, `apiKey` and `embedModel` to whatever that provider names the model.

## Building the index

`indexer.mjs` is not run by DSH — start it yourself, after the query side is configured. It must be able to `import` the `@deepseek-ai/*` packages, so run it with the DSH runtime (see below).

```bash
# layered: layer 1 (user messages) first, then layer 2 (assistant messages)
node indexer.mjs

node indexer.mjs --layer=1        # only user messages — fastest path to a usable search
node indexer.mjs --layer=2        # only assistant messages
node indexer.mjs --limit=200      # cap sessions this run
node indexer.mjs --status         # print progress, index nothing
node indexer.mjs --force          # re-index unchanged sessions
node indexer.mjs --quiet          # no progress lines, only key events
node indexer.mjs --skip-active=5  # skip sessions written in the last 5 minutes
```

| Environment variable | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `DSH_HOME` | `~/.dsh` | DSH home. Everything else derives from it. |
| `DSH_MODULES` | `$DSH_HOME/node_modules/@deepseek-ai` | Where to resolve `@deepseek-ai/*`. Override for the packaged desktop app. |
| `VEC_DB` | `$DSH_HOME/storages/session-query-vector.sqlite` | Index path — must equal the plugin's `path`. |
| `VEC_SESSIONS` | `$DSH_HOME/sessions` | Session log root. |
| `VEC_PROVIDER` | `ollama` | `ollama` or `openai` — must equal the plugin's `provider`. |
| `VEC_BASE_URL` | `http://127.0.0.1:11434` | Must equal the plugin's `baseUrl`. |
| `VEC_API_KEY` | `""` | Must equal the plugin's `apiKey`. |
| `VEC_MODEL` | `bge-m3` | Must equal the plugin's `embedModel`. |
| `VEC_CHUNK` | `1200` | Characters per chunk. |
| `VEC_BATCH` | `16` | Chunks per embedding request. |
| `VEC_SUBAGENTS` | — | Set to `1` to include subagent sessions. |

### Running the indexer against the packaged desktop app

The Electron app's `@deepseek-ai/*` modules live inside `app.asar`, which plain `node` cannot read. Point `DSH_MODULES` at the asar and run the indexer under the app's own binary in Node mode:

```powershell
$env:ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE = '1'
$env:DSH_MODULES = 'D:/APP/deepseek harness/resources/app.asar/dsh/node_modules/@deepseek-ai/'
& 'D:\APP\deepseek harness\DeepSeek Harness.exe' indexer.mjs --status
```

From a source checkout, plain `node indexer.mjs` works — `DSH_MODULES` already points at real files.

## Index schema

One SQLite file, `application_id = 1146308690` (distinct from the official backend's), `user_version = 1`. A file whose `application_id` belongs to something else is refused rather than clobbered.

| Table | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `vec_chunks(session_id, seq, type, time, chunk_idx, text, dim, vector BLOB)` | One row per embedded chunk. Primary key `(session_id, seq, chunk_idx)`. |
| `vec_sessions(id, revision, indexed_at, chunks, cwd, layer)` | Per-session bookkeeping; `revision` drives the incremental skip. |
| `vec_queries(text, vector, dim, at)` | Query-vector cache, so repeating a search skips the embedding round

plugins.description: DeepSeek Harness 插件：把全栈开发与问题排查提示词做成四个按场景自动加载的技能（单体/微服务 × 开发/排查），含 Vue3+TS+Spring Boot 与 Spring Cloud Alibaba 的硬约束。
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-agent-prompts

把「全栈开发 / 问题排查」提示词做成 **DeepSeek Harness 技能包**：装上之后不用再手动粘贴提示词，模型会在对的时候自己加载对应规范。

## 装了它解决什么问题

原来这些规范是几份长文档（单体 1978 行 + 微服务 2719 行）。用起来有三个麻烦：

1. 每次开新会话要重新贴，贴多了占上下文；
2. 四套提示词（单体开发 / 单体排查 / 微服务开发 / 微服务排查）混在两个文件里，靠人记哪个该用；
3. 里面有不少重复表述和不可判定的要求，真正执行时反而是噪音。

本插件把四套规范拆成四个**按场景触发**的技能，并做了压缩与结构化。

## 四个技能

| 技能 | 何时自动加载 |
|---|---|
| `fullstack-monolith-dev` | 单体全栈开发：Vue 3 + TS + Vite + Pinia / Spring Boot 3 + JDK 21 + MyBatis-Plus + Sa-Token |
| `fullstack-monolith-debug` | 单体应用故障排查（500/401/403/404、数据不一致、慢查询、连不上中间件） |
| `fullstack-microservice-dev` | 微服务开发：Spring Cloud Alibaba（Nacos / Gateway / OpenFeign / Sentinel / Seata）+ Maven 多模块 |
| `fullstack-microservice-debug` | 微服务链路排查（注册失败、网关 404、Feign 超时与 fallback 吞异常、熔断、Seata 不回滚、MQ 堆积） |

## 安装

harness 内（推荐，桌面 profile 只能走这条路）：

```
插件设置 → 安装 → 填入本包名或本地路径
```

或命令行（**只对 `web` profile 有效**；`desktop` profile 被 Electron 独占）：

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-agent-prompts
```

本地开发时可直接指向目录：

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add file:/path/to/dsh-agent-prompts
```

## 用法

装好后不需要任何操作。当你提出「新建一个 Spring Boot 项目」「这个接口 500 了帮我查」这类请求时，对应技能会出现在技能目录里，由模型按需加载。

也可以显式触发（在对话里说出技能名）：

```
用 fullstack-microservice-dev 规范帮我搭骨架
用 fullstack-monolith-debug 流程排查这个 500
```

## 相对原文档做了什么优化

| 项 | 原文档 | 本插件 |
|---|---|---|
| 结构 | 编号章节平铺，H1 混在中段 | 统一「前置 → 硬绑定 → 约定 → 流程 → 门禁 → 提问触发」 |
| 长度 | 单体 1978 行 / 微服务 2719 行 | 每个技能约 150–200 行 |
| 重复 | 环境变量、自检清单、禁止事项多处重复 | 去重，每个约束只出现一次 |
| 可判定性 | 部分要求无法判定（"注意代码质量"） | 一律改成可检查的断言或命令 |
| 自检清单 | 60+ 项勾选，实际不会逐条执行 | 压成「提交前门禁」8–10 条，每条对应一个可执行的验证 |
| 顺序 | 开发与排查混在同一文件 | 按「单体/微服务 × 开发/排查」四象限拆分 |
| 原文 | —— | 完整保留在 `reference/`，可随时对照 |

**没有删掉任何硬约束**：技术栈版本、四套环境、包结构、Feign 契约位置、网关规则、RBAC 要求、双文档同步、验证命令，全部保留并改写成了可执行形式。

## 目录

```
dsh-agent-prompts/
├── package.json
├── cordis.patch.yml           # profile 补丁：插入一条插件行
├── lib/index.js               # 注册四个技能
├── skills/                    # 技能正文（改文案不用改代码）
│   ├── fullstack-monolith-dev.md
│   ├── fullstack-monolith-debug.md
│   ├── fullstack-microservice-dev.md
│   └── fullstack-microservice-debug.md
└── reference/                 # 原始文档，逐字保留
    ├── fullstack-single.original.md
    └── fullstack-microservice.original.md
```

## 实现说明

- 纯 Host 插件，没有 client 半，因此不需要 `dsh.client` 字段，也不占侧边栏。
- `inject: ['skills']` 是硬依赖：技能服务不存在时插件不激活，不会出现"装了但没效果"。
- 技能正文运行时读盘（`skills/*.md`），改文案后重启即可生效，不用重新构建。
- 注册时 `source: 'bundled'`，`invocation` 同时允许模型与用户触发。

## 许可

MIT。`reference/` 下的原始文档版权归原作者，随包仅作对照用途。

plugins.description: Noema long-term memory plugin for DSH: durable, inspectable agent memory with recall tools and a settings page.
plugins.readme_text:
DSH Noema

Long-term memory for DeepSeek Harness — durable, inspectable agent memory backed by Noema.
Recall Before Work • Import From 9 Agent Tools • Settings-Page Memory Management • Crash Keep-Alive • Hot Reload

npm: @zseven-w/dsh-noema · Tested with DSH 0.2.0-rc.2

English · 简体中文 · 繁體中文 · 日本語 · 한국어 · Français · Español · Deutsch · Português · Русский · हिन्दी · Türkçe · ไทย · Tiếng Việt · Bahasa Indonesia


The Noema Memory settings page — import sources, memory management, and live server status

## Why DSH Noema DSH Noema connects [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) with [Noema](https://github.com/ZSeven-W/noema) — a local-first, non-vector memory system for coding agents — so an Agent keeps durable knowledge across sessions instead of starting every conversation from zero.
### 🧠 Durable Recall Memories persist as inspectable Markdown files under `NOEMA_ROOT` (default `~/.agent-memory/`). `noema_recall` loads relevant context at the start of a session; `noema_search`, `noema_browse`, `noema_catalog`, and `noema_recall_graph` cover lookup, exploration, and auditing. ### 📥 Import From Other Tools `noema_import` reads the memory files of ten other AI coding tools — Codex, Claude Code, opencode, Cursor, Grok, WorkBuddy, Antigravity, Trae, Qoder, Hermes — splits them into sections, and saves each as a durable memory. A content-keyed ledger deduplicates across runs and across tools that share files.
### 🛠️ Settings-Page Management The Noema Memory settings page configures the server command, memory root, budgets, idle/call timeouts, and the guidance section — and a Manage memories card searches, browses, adds, reviews, and deletes stored memories directly. ### 🩺 Keep-Alive The memory server stays up: idle timeout defaults to never, and a keep-alive loop restarts the `noema-mcp` child in the background when it crashes or exits, with a configurable check interval and restart backoff.
### 🔍 Smart Entity Extraction Noema's extraction engine combines jieba word segmentation with high-precision signals — English proper nouns, CJK names and technical terms, quoted topics, and repetition — with stopword and path filters, so the PageIndex topic catalog stays clean. ### ⚡ Hot Reload After the first boot, the plugin never needs a restart again: `pnpm run build` hot-reloads the host plugin through Cordis HMR, and `ppnpm run build:client` hot-swaps the browser bundle over the client-hmr SSE channel.
## Install into DSH ```sh dsh plugin --profile web add @zseven-w/dsh-noema@latest dsh web ``` Or, for local development straight from the source tree: ```sh dsh plugin --profile web add link:/path/to/dsh-noema dsh web ``` The `link:` protocol symlinks the profile dependency to this repository, so rebuilds are visible immediately and Cordis HMR can watch the compiled output. The plugin bundles the `noema-mcp` binary through per-platform optional npm packages. To build it yourself instead, run `cargo build --release -p noema-mcp` inside the bundled `noema` submodule, or point the Server command setting at any `noema-mcp` build. ## Memory Tools The model-facing tools mirror the Noema MCP surface: | Tool | What it does | | --- | --- | | `noema_recall` | Recall relevant memories for a query, with a token budget. | | `noema_search` | Full-text search over stored memories. | | `noema_browse` | Browse the PageIndex catalog for a topic or entity. | | `noema_catalog` | Render the full memory catalog as markdown. | | `noema_recall_graph` | Multi-hop recall through links and shared entities. | | `noema_neighbors` | One graph hop from a memory. | | `noema_explain` | Explain why a memory was or was not recalled. | | `noema_remember` | Save a durable fact, decision, constraint, or preference. | | `noema_review_list` | List pending review candidates. | | `noema_review_decide` | Accept, reject, edit, or merge a candidate. | | `noema_forget` | Tombstone or hard-delete a memory. | | `noema_policy_get` / `noema_policy_set` | Read or update the write policy. | | `noema_status` | Server and tenant status: counts, index health, storage root. | | `noema_import` | Import memories from other AI coding tools. | Each tool returns a uniform envelope `{ ok, tool, text }` where `text` carries the full server output. ## Import memories from other tools | Source id | Global files | Workspace files | | --- | --- | --- | | `codex` | `~/.codex/AGENTS.md` + the Codex memory pipeline: `~/.codex/memories/MEMORY.md`, `memory_summary.md`, `rollout_summaries/*.md`, `extensions/ad_hoc/notes/*.md` (`raw_memories.md` skipped — it is the uncurated feed) | `AGENTS.md`, `AGENTS.local.md` | | `claude-code` | `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`, `~/.claude/CLAUDE.local.md`, `~/.claude/MEMORY.md` | `CLAUDE.md`, `CLAUDE.local.md`, `MEMORY.md` | | `opencode` | `~/.config/opencode/AGENTS.md` | `AGENTS.md` | | `cursor` | `~/.cursor/rules/*.mdc`, `~/.cursorrules` | `.cursor/rules/*.mdc`, `.cursorrules` | | `grok` | `~/.grok/AGENTS.md` + the Grok cross-session memory: `~/.grok/memory/MEMORY.md`, per-project `MEMORY.md`, and `sessions/*.md` summaries | `AGENTS.md` | | `workbuddy` | `~/.codebuddy/CODEBUDDY.md` (WorkBuddy memory file), `~/.workbuddy/AGENTS.md`, `~/.workbuddy/memory.md`, `~/.config/workbuddy/AGENTS.md`, `~/Library/Application Support/WorkBuddy/AGENTS.md` | `AGENTS.md`, `CODEBUDDY.md` | | `antigravity` | `~/.antigravity/AGENTS.md`, `~/.config/antigravity/AGENTS.md`, `~/Library/Application Support/Antigravity/AGENTS.md` (best-effort; no documented global memory store yet) | `AGENTS.md`, `AGENTS.local.md` | | `trae` | `~/.trae/AGENTS.md`, `~/.trae/memory/`, `~/.trae/rules/` (plus the `~/.trae-cn` variants) | `AGENTS.md`, `.trae/rules/` | | `qoder` | `~/.qoder-cn/AGENTS.md`, `~/.qoder-cn/rules/`, the auto-memory roots `~/.qoder-cn/memory/` and `~/.qoder-cn/projects/*/memory/` (plus `~/.qoder` variants) | `AGENTS.md`, `AGENTS.local.md`, `.qoder/rules/` | | `hermes` | `~/.hermes/memories/` (`MEMORY.md` + `USER.md`) and the global `~/.hermes/SOUL.md` | `.hermes.md`, `HERMES.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md` | - The `source` argument selects one tool, or omit it to run every source enabled in settings. - The `path` argument selects the workspace root for project-scoped files (defaults to the session workspace; workspace files only load when the Import workspace files setting is on). - Imports are deduplicated through a ledger at `$DSH_HOME/storages/dsh-noema-imports.json`, keyed by file path +
